newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Foreigners may avoid Ukraine T-bill tax.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners may avoid Ukraine T-bill tax.

text.p: Foreigners investing in Ukraine's Treasury bills may be saved from paying a 30 percent tax on profits if their countries hold mutual taxation agreements with Ukraine, a senior Finance Minister official said on Wednesday.

"Legal entities, both residents and non-residents, will pay the same tax on profits earned from buying T-bills, unless there is a mutual taxation agreement saving them from double taxation," Deputy Finance Minister Vasyl Rehuretsky told an economic conference.
The new law is due to take effect on July 1. Until now profits earned from T-bill buying have been tax-free.
Rehuretsky said Ukraine holds about 20 taxation agreements with other countries and most contain clauses which would significantly lower the tax or remove it altogether.
The deputy minister said the government was considering implementing a tax holiday on T-bill profits to 2000.
Yields at sales this week stood at between 20.00 and 30.75 percent for six-month, nine-month and 12-month T-bills.
